newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB sells no wheat in tender 23, now lists reserve.
newsitem.headline: AWB sells no wheat in tender 23, now lists reserve.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said it sold no wheat in its latest tender for sales from its national pool.
Total bids were received for 56,000 tonnes of current crop wheat and for 6,000 tonnes of 1997/98 season wheat, it said.

AWB also listed for the first time its reserve prices for Australian Standard White (ASW) wheat, which showed that latest highest unsuccessful bids were between A$5 and A$16 a tonne less than prices the AWB was prepared to accept for current crop wheat and A$29 a tonne less than its reserve for new crop wheat.

The next tender would be held on May 28, AWB said.
Note: ASW = Australian Standard White; APH = Australian Prime Hard; AH1 = Australian Hard 1; APW = Australian Premium White.
